rationale: PLAN_2026-08-11 step 5 (webdesign_uk_build_service lane), deployer half. Migration 406 gates the SUGGESTION of a requires-backend tool (tool-suggester only offers it to sites whose deploy_config capabilities include 'backend'); nothing gates the DEPLOY. deploy_tool_to_site is driven by add_tool work items from any source — a human, an older suggestion minted before 406, a replayed item — so a requires-backend tool (today: chat-input-box, the only tool-level row carrying the tag) could still be forked onto a static site, shipping a widget that POSTs same-origin to an /api/ endpoint the site does not have. The widget fails closed by design, so the failure is a permanently dead chat box that every status surface reads as a successful deploy. This change (1) refuses that deploy BEFORE any write, using 406's own capability predicate byte-for-byte (the pin-predicate-vs-pool-predicate divergence is a filed landmine class); (2) also refuses when the target site has zero current evidence_base facts, because the site-facts relay (internal/core-manager/handlers/sitefacts.go) serves 404 without them and the chat binary refuses to start on zero facts — a provision request minted for such a site would be unsatisfiable at birth, which is bugs_open/177's exact class (9 of 9 tool_content items ever minted died in needs_human_review for the same born-unsatisfiable shape); (3) on a successful fresh deploy, raises ONE handler-less backend_provision work item (status needs_human_review, the TL-032/TL-042 posture) as the handover to the operator, because the in-cluster pipeline cannot reach the off-cluster box by design (PLAN_2026-08-11 §4 Option A's isolation posture) and must not pretend to provision what it cannot. The item's spec names the token secret (SITE_FACTS_TOKEN) and never carries its value — a work-item row is readable by every agent on the fleet. recurrenceExpected is set because this is an action request: a completed provision is a SUCCESS, and the two-strike rule would otherwise brand a third legitimate re-ask terminal 'unresolved' at birth (bugs_open/024; the LANDMINES recurrenceExpected entry). The new item type follows owner ruling 2026-08-02 §1: its producer set (DeployToolToSiteAction only, fresh-deploy arm only) and item_key shape (backend_provision:<tool_function>:<site_id>) are named in a concept-register entry (TL-043, tool-lifecycle.md) shipped in the same commit; VMB-010 is cross-updated. RFC_022 shape check: the gate is opt-in by tag (2 components fleet-wide carry requires-backend, 1 tool-level), the unsafe side (no gate) was the previous default and the change only ever REFUSES deploys that could not work or ADDS an item — no live deployer-created requires-backend fork exists (webdesign.uk's chat box is a hand splice on the contact page, not a deployer fork), so zero existing behaviour changes. Consumers told: the tool-suggester side already carries the same predicate (406); tool-generator's create_tool_component arm is deliberately out of scope and named in TL-043 as a known gap — it mints NEW tools and writes their tags itself, so it cannot deploy the existing requires-backend library tool. Known test gap stated honestly: the action-level wiring (tag -> gate -> raise, 8 lines) has no full-action test; the three helpers are unit-tested (the recurrence flag mutation-proven: flipping it fails the by-effect test) and the wiring is proven by the PLAN step 5 second-site acceptance run. Documentation shipped in the same commit, not listed as edits per runbook guidance: register TL-043 (new), VMB-010 update, 000_concept_index row.

plan.summary: deploy_tool_to_site gains the deploy-time half of the requires-backend gate: refuse (before any write) a requires-backend tool aimed at a site without the backend capability or without current evidence_base facts, and on a successful fresh deploy raise one handler-less backend_provision work item handing the box-side provisioning to the operator, with the raise disposition surfaced in the action's output map.

edits.rationale: New file holding the gate's four pieces, each separately testable. toolRequiresBackend parses semantic_tags with a fail-safe fallback (a malformed column must not disarm the gate — the unsafe side is a widget deployed against no backend). loadBackendEligibility mirrors 406's capability predicate and the relay's facts predicate byte-for-byte. backendEligibilityRefusal is the decision extracted from the action so the refusal is proven by test rather than asserted by comment. raiseBackendProvisionItem goes through the shared withWorkItemTx door (the council has already ruled against hand-rolled ON CONFLICT inserts, corr a5b70424) with recurrenceExpected set.

Wire the gate at the one chokepoint every library-tool deploy passes through. Step 1b runs after the tool load and BEFORE the fork-existence check, so an ineligible site gets a refusal with nothing written. Step 5b raises the provision item right after the page_component insert (the moment the widget is live), fresh-deploy arm only — the already-deployed backfill arm deliberately does not re-mint, because the backend is already running. The output map carries backend_required always and the raise disposition when required: a requires-backend tool whose provision request was never filed is a permanently dead widget that reads as a successful deploy everywhere else.

The refusals proven on the extracted decision function (including the malformed-tags fail-safe and the superstring non-match); the insert pinned on the fields that make the row routable (item_type backend_provision, empty handler_agent, needs_human_review status, 16 args); the recurrence flag proven by EFFECT exactly as tool_content_item_test.go proves it — mutation-verified this session: flipping recurrenceExpected to false fails TestRaiseBackendProvisionItem_RecurrenceExpected_SurvivesTerminalPredecessors with disposition insert_failed. No not-issued-query assertions (the LANDMINES entry on insertWorkItem's vacuous negatives).

plan.risks: Zero live behaviour changes on the deployed estate: no deployer-created requires-backend fork exists (the tag census is 2 components, and webdesign.uk's live chat box is a hand splice, not a deployer fork), so every existing deploy path is byte-identical — the gate activates only on the tag. The refusal changes the already-deployed early-return for a requires-backend tool on a site that LOST its capability (refusal instead of already_deployed:true) — measured reachable by zero current rows. The relay-base constant is advisory config in a work-item spec, not a wire dependency; the route registration in core-manager remains the authority. The action-level wiring has no full-action test (stated in the rationale); the second-site acceptance run covers it.
